events.description: Needle biopsy with poorly differentiated squamous carcinoma on pathology

events.description: PD-L1 detection with tumor proportion score

evidence.quote: The specimen was sent for PD-L1 detection and tumor proportion score (TPS) was 80%, indicating a high expression of PD-L1.

events.description: Neoadjuvant gemcitabine plus cisplatin chemotherapy started, pembrolizumab added from the second cycle

events.description: Adverse effects during neoadjuvant treatment, treated symptomatically

evidence.quote: During the treatment, the adverse effects in this patient included vomiting, thrombocytopenia, and occasional chest distress.

summary.text: A 57-year-old man with a dry cough for more than one month was admitted to thoracic surgery; he had a smoking history of over 20 years, a history of hemorrhoids, no prior surgery and no family history of tumor, with a physical status score of 0.

Chest CT and PET-CT on 9 October 2019 showed two left lower lobe masses, one adjacent to the left hilum and one on the basal segment, with increased metabolic activity, considered malignant, and no distant metastatic signs; brain MRI showed no abnormal signs.

Needle biopsy showed poorly differentiated squamous carcinoma with PD-L1 TPS of 80%; mediastinal staging was not performed because the patient refused invasive examinations. Clinical stage was cT2aN1M0, IIB, and pneumonectomy was the considered surgery plan.

He received five cycles of neoadjuvant gemcitabine plus cisplatin from October 2019 to March 2020 with pembrolizumab added from the second cycle; the plan was suspended after the fourth cycle because of COVID-19. CT after two and four cycles showed shrinking masses, and adverse effects of vomiting, thrombocytopenia and occasional chest distress were alleviated with symptomatic treatment.

PET-CT on 28 April 2020 showed smaller masses with SUVmax of 8.4 for each. Left lower lobectomy on 30 April 2020 was followed by pathology with no detected tumor in the resected mass or lymph nodes, a pathologic complete response, and the operation was changed from the planned pneumonectomy to lobectomy.

At postoperative follow-up on 2 June 2020 there were no recurrent or metastatic signs. He refused postoperative chemotherapy but received intravenous pembrolizumab 200 mg on four dates from June to August 2020, with mild cough, vomiting and decreased platelet counts that were alleviated; CA-125 and CEA were measured serially through August 2020.

article_limitations: Figure pixels are reviewed in visual.json; the annotation figure rows keep caption-only status.
Figure 4 prints the first postoperative CA-125/CEA values under a different date than the text; those two facts are review_only with an ambiguity.
The source states further data were not available after the last tumor marker measurement; no later follow-up is documented.
Chemotherapy cycle dates printed only inside Figure 4 are pixel content and are not used as facts.
Pembrolizumab route for the neoadjuvant doses is not stated and is left unset.
No literal order links the presentation, brain MRI, postoperative adverse effects or the year-less tumor-marker dates to other events.
